steps.content: You pull out a chair and sit, lifting your eyes to meet Margaret's. A faint, knowing smile rests on her lips, her posture perfectly poised. From her refined makeup to the elegant line of her dress, she is an image of flawless, unassailable grace.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Morning, Margaret. Hope the Bureau didn't treat you too poorly for your first night here.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Good morning, Chief. I rested well, thank you. Though... and I hope this doesn't come across as rude... I would still very much prefer this to be my only stay here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This interrogation room's for finding answers, not making things hard. Ms. Margaret, if you're honest with me, and you're innocent, we'll both get what we need.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: How reassuring. It seems we share the same goal. I couldn't ask for better. If only my so-called colleagues in Fraser were half as agreeable, my work would be far simpler.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I've always believed honesty enables dialogue, and dialogue enables mutual peace. But as my presence here suggests... not everyone shares that belief. It appears quite a few "friends" hold rather different convictions.
Margaret's face breaks into a genuine smile. The polished, diplomatic distance vanishes at once, replaced by a warmth and ease you didn't sense in her yesterday.
Sinners brought to the interrogation room are typically guarded, defensive. Margaret is only open. You can't quite decipher her angle, so for now, you keep probing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Maybe those who aren't honest themselves assume openness is just another act? Or maybe it's like me. Do this job long enough, and you get professionally suspicious.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Most people avoid talking about their failures, but you brought yours up yourself. When someone breaks the pattern, I have to wonder... what are you hoping to gain?
Your direct question catches Margaret off guard for a second. But there's no sign of panic, only a light, amused laugh as she raises a hand to her lips.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Then I'm afraid you've misread me. You're someone even the steely Langley speaks well of, and you've seen my file. I'm sure my little secrets are already laid bare before you.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I assumed my maneuvering wouldn't escape your notice, so I chose candor, hoping it might earn your goodwill... and perhaps an earlier release. I didn't expect it would work against me.
Her openness in admitting her own calculations surprises you. However, it's the mention of your former superior's name that truly catches your attention.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Really? She "spoke well" of me? I didn't take Madam Langley for the type to discuss work with friends. Not many Paradeisos nobles choose to get their hands dirty. Is that what connected you two?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Hmm... To be honest, it's difficult to say if Langley and I are friends. Even if I claimed we were, her answer might differ. We have differing perspectives, after all. Friction is inevitable.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I suppose we are peers, more than anything. Kindred spirits, in a way. The sort who might lend a hand if circumstances allow—to one another, and to those who follow, like yourself.

Margaret rests the tip of her fan lightly against her cheek, considering your question. Her sincerity feels genuine, and her decision not to invoke her ties to Langley earns a subtle shift in your regard.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Mind if I ask what kind of friction? Just so we're clear. Are we talking "I'm a Fraser spy and she wants me dead," or more like "we disagree on which foot to put through the door first"?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: How humorous you are! But rest assured, I am no spy, nor have I ever accepted a single coin from Fraser. There's no need to trouble Langley and that gun of hers.
Your teasing draws a soft laugh from her. Sensing you've started to lower your guard, she meets your lightness with a playful quip of her own.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Simply put, she sometimes finds me too naive, and I occasionally find her too pragmatic. Surely you've had similar... disagreements with her?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I imagine she sometimes sees me as a child throwing a fit. But you as well? You both came of age in turbulent times. You traveled the farlands with your father, an Outland Affairs Officer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Oppression, independence, expansion, stability... DisCity has gone through a lot, and so have its people. It's only natural that she and I see things differently. But the DisCity you witnessed... shouldn't it be closer to the one Madam Langley knows?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: In Langley's words... perhaps I am too much of a dreamer. I know, no matter how much changes, chaos and conflict remain the themes of this city, of this world. And yet, I still believe...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It is precisely because the world is this way that peace must remain our common pursuit. Our most fundamental one.
A flicker of bitterness crosses her smile, there and gone. What remains is a fierce, unmistakable resolve.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This "too naive" dream of yours... Is it peace?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes. It sounds like such a grand word, the sort an Outland Affairs Officer should champion. But to me, it has always been something... much more personal.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It's been a long time since I've spoken of what it truly means. Since you ask... would you care to hear it?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can't think of a reason to say no. But may I ask... why tell me?

You watch Margaret weigh her words carefully, as if gathering her courage. For once, the unflappable Outland Affairs Officer seems less than sure. And in that vulnerability, you know this is where the real story begins.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Because I've heard how you stabilized the West District and reopened the Hypercube mine. How you thwarted an Outland spy ring from undermining DisCity, and prevented BR-002 and BR-005 from causing far greater harm.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: None of that was easy, and yet you've come this far. My own work in Fraser has been... fraught. But whenever my spirit wavered, word of your deeds would find its way to me. It lifted me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're talking about... me?
Margaret nods, her expression earnest.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes, you. You showed me I am not alone in believing this road leads somewhere hopeful. We may have started in different places, seen through different eyes, but we've both witnessed what the Black Rings and war leave in their wake. We both want it to end.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Traveling with my father changed me for the rest of my life. It showed me the suffering of ordinary people—something one never sees in Paradeisos—and it showed me the power of peace, of words.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Truthfully, my father rarely prevailed against entrenched interests, and he faced constant danger. But on those few occasions he succeeded... countless lives were spared from war and torment.
Her voice holds a note of wistfulness, of memory held close. For a moment, you can almost see the girl she used to be, deeply moved by something she was too young to fully grasp.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I wanted to be like him. That is why I returned to Paradeisos, why I left again for Fraser. Every path I've walked has been for that simple purpose. But such an ideal... it is delicate. Fragile.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Sometimes I waver. I wonder if I truly am too naive. You may not realize it, but your actions have mended my missteps and encouraged me to keep going. For that, I must thank you.

As a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, her eloquence is no surprise. But her eyes speak more plainly; they are brimming with emotions too layered to name. You can feel their weight, the depth of her regard for you.
Faced with such an unguarded confession, your cheeks flush. You clear your throat, gently breaking the moment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You'd never even met me. For all you knew, I could've been some glory-seeker playing hero, someone who didn't care about peace at all.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Have you forgotten? I am not merely an Outland Affairs Officer, Chief. Since going undercover in Fraser to investigate Outland collusion with the Underground... I've seen my share of arrogant foxes and greedy hyenas.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: In diplomacy or covert work, any partnership requires common interest. Who comes out ahead in the end... well, that comes down to skill. I may not look it, but there are few who can match me.
As if sensing your bashfulness, Margaret gives a soft chuckle, a flicker of mischief in her gaze. She deftly dismantles the tender atmosphere she had just spun.
It's a considerate pivot, yet one that feels just as honest. You decide to match her openness with your own.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I understand your ideals. What I don't understand is why you became a secret agent. You could've followed your father's path. Just be a proper Outland Affairs Officer. Wouldn't that have served the same goal?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When you call yourself naive, it's only relative to other agents, isn't it? I know you've had blood on your hands. I've read that you've been forced to leave people behind. Why choose to carry that?
The question lands like a touch to a bruise. Her expression tightens—a subtle, involuntary flinch—and she looks down, lost in a memory or a thought.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: To be honest... I thought the same for a long time. I refused to join Langley's 9th Agency. I told her I wanted no part in that kind of work.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Back then, I believed an ideal peace could only be won through ideal means—that anything less would stain it beyond recognition. But that... pristine little conviction of mine didn't last long.
A shadow settles in her eyes as she says it, darkening her features.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I wonder... if you recall the previous <color=#fb9259>Great Expo</color>.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You mean the one where <color=#fb9259>BR-003</color> broke out?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes. I was an Outland Affairs Officer stationed in Fraser at the time. I had spent years laying the groundwork, carefully persuading them to attend. I truly believed it would mark a new beginning for peace.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But when I returned to DisCity with the delegation, ready to celebrate what we'd achieved... the Black Ring took everything. I didn't even have time to grieve. I was quietly conscripted, granted special clearance to become an advocate for weaponizing the Black Ring.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I never believed the rhetoric, that weapons of deterrence could bring peace. But if not me, it would have been someone else. I swallowed my anger and told myself that at least with me involved, I could set limits. Soften the edges. Find room to maneuver.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I fought to impose strict conditions on its use, then leveraged that to reduce stockpiles of weapons designed for mass civilian casualties. I told myself... some things cannot be done with clean hands.
A ripple of weariness passes over her features, betraying the real scars beneath the carefully constructed mask of history. This isn't a performance. This is something true, painfully so.
The shadow of regret remains, unhidden, in her expression. But as you extend a gesture of understanding, her smile resurfaces, graceful and composed once more.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Thank you. When it was over, I declined their offer to stay. Instead, I requested a transfer back to Fraser. DisCity's vision of peace had... diverged too far from my own. I thought Fraser might be a better stage for what I hoped to achieve.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: What came after... well, you can read it in my file. An Outland Affairs Officer is always viewed with suspicion in Fraser. But fortunately, I had an excellent role model who helped me find my footing, barely.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There's nothing "barely" about your record. From infiltration to building a network, every move was impressively precise. You became DisCity's most valuable asset in Fraser. But that's exactly why any slip-up makes them suspicious.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The farlands gained independence, Fraser was denied the Hypercubes, and it ended peacefully—an outcome that still favored DisCity. Even if it was your "slip-up," holding it against you seems... pretty greedy.
You understand, perhaps too clearly, the choices pressed upon her, the wars she gave everything to. Something tightens in your chest, a deep and genuine ache of empathy.
Noticing you've taken her side, Margaret seems to soften. A true smile touches her eyes, and her tone lifts, lightened by a hint of relief.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I'm so glad we see it the same way. I had a feeling we might. But there are always those who miss the bigger picture, people who see nothing beyond their own gain, yet insist on meddling and throwing everything into chaos.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You sound like you've been through this before. Is this not your first interrogation?
She pauses, her cheeks puffing out just a touch. For a fleeting moment, she looks almost girlish, making no attempt to mask her flash of petulance.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Naturally... Both DisCity and Fraser have too many nobles and officials blind to the common people. To them, casualty figures mean nothing. The only numbers that matter are the ones in their accounts.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: We lay our plans so carefully, negotiate a result... only for the hyenas to come snapping at our heels, eager to overturn the table. It happens far too often. Just thinking about it makes my blood boil.
In this moment, the woman before you seems a world apart from the flawless DisCity Outland Affairs Officer you first met. This is simply Margaret: vivid, human, and real. You can't help but smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So you do get angry.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I'm only human, Chief. Peace is... a little hobby of mine. A private indulgence. Destroying it is like trampling a garden I've lovingly tended. Of course, I get angry.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But such frustrations pass. What truly pains me is friction with kindred spirits. Working toward the same goal, yet getting in each other's way, unable to accomplish anything... That is what I find truly regrettable.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you saying... you and Madam Langley have had that kind of friction as well?
You ask out of genuine curiosity, expecting a lighthearted story. What follows is anything but.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: No, I'm referring to the recent farland independence. Sigh... I was quite fond of the young Campbell girl. Such determination and talent. I even arranged a suitable position for her within the Farland Alliance...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But I didn't expect her cleverness to become a double-edged sword, leading the farland people away from the path I had envisioned. If this continues, it will be difficult for me to offer them further assistance. Theirs will become a road of thorns...
Margaret speaks with such casual candor that it takes you a moment to register the full gravity of what she's said.
You stop her, your mind already rewinding, scanning for anything you might have missed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The farland independence? The young Campbell girl... You mean Hypatia? Adelaide's sister? You arranged a position for her in the Alliance?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you telling me that all of this was part of your plan from the beginning?
She meets your gaze, her gentle sincerity unwavering. There is no guilt in her eyes, only a steady, open calm.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes. I have no reason to hide it from you. Many details unfolded in ways I had not foreseen, but the outcome still aligned with my design. For that... I am reasonably satisfied.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You're admitting it, just like that? Nothing else you want to explain to defend yourself?

Your thoughts snag for a moment. But on reflection, she never truly tried to cover her motives. She was open about her ideological rift with DisCity's leadership, and clear that her role in Fraser was more than a simple posting.
But what unsettles you most isn't her staggering confession. It's your own reaction: your first impulse wasn't to report her; it was to listen.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I could explain, but do you truly need me to? I imagine even from the fragments my old colleague shared, you can already piece together the full picture.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes. Fraser's role as the puppet master was exposed. The Farland Alliance gained independence. A people struggling to survive now have a Hypercube mine to call their own. This is the situation I engineered.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: What I did has certainly harmed DisCity's interests. It could be called "treason." But all I wanted was for the Hypercubes the farlanders paid for with their lives to belong to their comrades and their children.
Margaret holds your gaze without faltering, her eyes clear with conviction and trust. Even now, she maps the journey her heart has taken and offers you a place beside her.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I wanted the newly discovered Hypercube mine to belong to an independent third party—one that desires peace—to help stabilize the standoff between the two powers. Not Fraser the oppressor, nor DisCity with its overflowing reserves.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Chief, if you were in my position—the farlanders' struggle before you, the oppression of Fraser and DisCity behind you—what would you choose?
Caught in the tide of the moment, the answer almost slips free, but you bite it back. She doesn't press.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I won't press you or rush your answer. I'm simply doing what I have done from the start: laying myself bare before you, hoping to earn your support. Because I believe that if I am to change anything... you are my only hope.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But in the end, this is only my side of the story. Whatever you decide, I will understand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're openly telling me you want to win me over. Aren't you worried I'll see it as manipulation and report you on the spot?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I believe honesty is the only path to trust, just as I believe peace is the only soil in which civilization can flourish. If you truly give me no chance at all... I will accept that graciously.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: If you believe I should be punished for the goals I've pursued and the things I've done, then so be it. This was my decision, and I do not fear paying the price.

She watches you fall into reflection and makes no move to pull you back. The stillness grows heavy, measured only by your indecision. You weigh her confession again and again, still uncertain whether to accept it as truth or reject it as artifice.
Perhaps you need to step outside the emotional current Margaret has drawn you into, just for a moment. To think with a clearer head.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You're right. Your motives, your actions, their consequences—everything I've heard is only your side. I need more information before I can decide.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But it's been a long time since you've returned to DisCity, and I shouldn't keep you here. How about this: you accept the shackles, I grant you clearance to free movement, and we both give each other some time?
Lamia

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Chief, you still remember your promise and truly intend to keep me here for just one night. It's very considerate of you. I certainly won't refuse.

With a playful quip, she slips off her gloves without pause and offers her hand in an unshielded gesture. Your fingers meet hers: only warmth, only steadiness. Just what you have already begun to believe.

Crimson spikes of light shimmer into existence. You reach through the connection and feel only the same calm gentleness she projects—a silent confirmation that the woman before you is precisely who she seems: clear-hearted, devoted wholly to good. By every measure, you should help her.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Hehe... I never expected the shackles to feel quite like this. It's as though you're always by my side, cheering me on. How reassuring.
Yet as she rises with fluid grace and moves past you, a knot tightens in your gut:
Could someone of her caliber—a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer and veteran spy—truly be so transparent? Would she so easily hand you the power to decide her fate?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Oh, right, the cameras...
As your gaze shifts, it catches on the surveillance equipment, and you remember the recording. You hesitate, weighing the choice.

Leave it, and Margaret's political enemies could seize the footage at any moment, stripping you of room to maneuver. Delete it, and you've effectively taken her side, limiting your options just as surely.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, has the interrogation ended? IT just reported a malfunction in the surveillance equipment. The footage from the second half wasn't recorded.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: We should have notified you immediately, but the alert itself was... delayed, for reasons currently unexplained.
Well, there's the answer. How convenient the system chose now to fail. You shake your head, wondering: could the timing really be so perfect?
